chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man whom the Imam paused for the Lian (cursing). He testified with two testimonies, then withdrew and lied about himself before finishing the Lian. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped the Hadd of the slanderer, and he is not separated from his wife.'

key_terms.حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ: The Hadd (fixed punishment) of the slanderer
key_terms.لِلِّعَانِ: Lian (oath of cursing between husband and wife)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband withdraws his Lian testimony and admits lying before it is finished?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of a husband who interrupts the Lian procedure by retracting his testimony before completion, ruling that he receives the fixed punishment for slander (Qadhf) and remains married to his wife. This contrasts with the standard outcome of Lian, which typically results in permanent separation, highlighting the significance of the timing of the withdrawal in Shia jurisprudence. The ruling underscores the principle that incomplete Lian does not trigger the full marital dissolution associated with its completion.
